components.basis: Tail definition, empty-family convention, uniform small-event control, E(Z;A) notation and the version convention are stated. Durrett's variant (definition for an arbitrary collection, p. 244) and his remark sup E|X_i| <= M+1 are preserved and proved equivalent to the handbook form.

Both directions, the dominated-family case (Durrett's 'trivial example', p. 244), the finite-family case and the worked boundary (n 1_(0,1/n): bounded first moments without uniform integrability) are proved.

Criterion, both source examples and the convex converse are proved. Durrett's Theorem 4.6.2 form (any phi >= 0, bound E phi(|X_i|) <= C, epsilon_M = sup{x/phi(x): x >= M}, no integrability assumed) is preserved and proved; boundaries (phi(x)=x fails, non-uniform bound fails, criterion not necessary) are worked.

Theorem 4.6.1 for every sub-sigma-algebra; proof written (small-event control of |X|, Markov, conditional Jensen, defining identity on {E(|X| | G) > M}); the source's 'very large family' point is the no-nesting/no-countability remark.
All five assertions proved, including Lemma 4.6.5 (uniformly in A) and the infinite-expectation case of the Fatou form.

Theorem 4.6.3 with hypothesis E|X_n| < infinity, convergence in probability, all three implications; both source truncations (clipping phi_M, cutoff psi_M linear on [M-1,M]) are written, including the earlier-index step.

components.gap: Supply thm:p15-submartingale-ui without an unstated assumption (failure condition: unstated assumption; the identified source variant, Durrett's Theorem 4.6.4 for adapted submartingales, p. 246, is not preserved). The annex proof (handbook/annex/p15/uniform-integrability-and-conditional-limits.tex 204-207 and 219-221) uses that every X_n is F_n-measurable: it calls the finite-convergence event and the chosen limit X_infinity F_infinity-measurable because 'limsup and liminf of the measurable variables are measurable', and it treats {E(X_infinity|F_n) - X_n <= -1/k} as an F_n-event. Neither the theorem (body 110-121) nor def:p15-filtration-martingale (handbook/parts/p15/martingales-and-convergence.tex 15-33), which defines adaptedness but does not require it of a submartingale or supermartingale, states adaptedness, and no convention on the route before this chapter supplies it (the convention 'Processes are real and adapted' appears only later, in def:p15-os-conventions of the optional-stopping chapter). State adaptedness as a hypothesis (in the theorem, or by repairing the definition, packet duty MP-0 of 162.1), or write proofs of the F_infinity-measurable choice of the limit and of X_n <= E(X_infinity|F_n) that do not use it.

components.basis: Closing variable defined (source Theorem 4.6.7 (iv)); F_infinity and the non-measurability boundary are stated and used in thm:p15-closed-martingale.

components.gap: Supply thm:p15-closed-martingale without an unstated assumption (failure condition: unstated assumption). The annex proof (handbook/annex/p15/uniform-integrability-and-conditional-limits.tex 228-235 and 239-240) states 'Since X_n is integrable and F_n-measurable, it is a version of E(X_infinity|F_n)' and reuses 'the F_infinity-measurable limit version constructed above' from the submartingale proof; both require each X_n to be F_n-measurable. The handbook's martingale definition (def:p15-filtration-martingale, handbook/parts/p15/martingales-and-convergence.tex 15-33) does not require adaptedness, so X_n is only almost surely equal to the F_n-measurable E(X_{n+1}|F_n), and neither the theorem (body 132-143) nor its proof states or derives the measurability it uses. State adaptedness as a hypothesis (or repair the definition, packet duty MP-0 of 162.1), or write the version argument (X_n = E(X_{n+1}|F_n) almost surely, and an F_infinity-measurable version of the limit built from those versions).

components.basis: Theorem 4.6.8 a.s. and in L^1; versions chosen adapted; source identification step (pi-system union, lambda-system) written; exceptional-set definition of the limit given.
Theorem 4.6.9 and the source's Kolmogorov zero-one argument are proved; Chung's line, the 'obvious' and 'incredible' readings and Durrett's evaluation (pp. 247--248) are given.

Exercise 4.6.7 and Theorem 4.6.10 (with the source's W_N proof, null sets combined countably) are proved, plus L^1 for the dominated case; the source title 'dominated convergence theorem for conditional expectations' is recorded.

All three examples are proved; item 3 is Example 4.6.11 (B_n, C_n with X_n = n B_n C_n equals Durrett's Y_n Z_n), with UI, a.s. and L^1 limits, the conditional identity and the a.s. failure via both Borel--Cantelli lemmas.
Durrett's setting for Exercises 4.6.2--3 (Omega=[0,1), I_{k,n}, sigma(I_{k,n})) with uniform probability and the endpoint remark.

Exercises 4.6.2 and 4.6.3 in full (martingale property, a.s. and L^1 convergence, integral identity for all 0<=a<=b<=1 with the endpoint extension, step approximation, completed-measurability extension); Durrett's remark comparing Exercise 1.4.3 is given.

Exercise 4.6.1 (i.i.d. integrable noise, independent integrable theta) proved a.s. and in L^1; the normal reading, prior and posterior distributions and the posterior-mean version are supplied; the boundary (additive model only) is stated.
Exercise 4.6.4 (delta_K for positive integers K is equivalent to Durrett's delta(x)) and Exercise 4.6.5 (p_0 > 0, natural filtration, initial extinction included, no mean assumption) are proved.
Exercise 4.6.6 with adaptedness stated: martingale property, limit in {0,1}, P(X_inf=1)=EX_0 and the deterministic theta case, plus realizability.
Reverse-time definition with measurability, tower consequence, G_infinity, and Durrett's negative-index form E(X_{k+1}|F_k)=X_k for k<=-1; the name 'reversed' is recorded.

Theorems 4.7.1--4.7.2: upcrossings of each finite reversed string, monotone count, a.s. finite limit, UI via Y_n = E(Y_0|G_n), L^1, G_infinity-measurable version, identification; Durrett's simplicity claim is explained.
Theorem 4.7.3 proved from the backward theorem with the tower identity; finite-dimensional extension proved.

defect_observations: C010 body 156-158 and C021 body 351-354: the end-of-statement \cite (thm. 4.6.8; thm. 4.7.3) directly follows handbook additions (definition of the limit on the exceptional set; the finite-dimensional vector extension and the remark on uncountable coordinate families) that are not in Durrett's theorems; the attribution reads as covering them. Verdict unaffected (the theorem statements themselves are Durrett's).

C007 annex 207 and C020 annex 604: Vitali's theorem (hypothesis: convergence in probability) is applied right after almost-sure convergence without citing the almost-sure-to-probability step (proved at thm:p15-w02b-p15-013-comparison (1)). Minor citation omission, not a missing argument.
C016 body 257 calls the noise mean 'known'; Durrett's Exercise 4.6.1 assumes only E|Z_i| < infinity. The word adds no mathematical restriction (mu = E Z_1, as the supplement says at 804-805).
C017 body 276-281 uses delta_K for positive integers K where Durrett's Exercise 4.6.4 has delta(x); the two hypotheses are equivalent (take K = max(1, ceiling of x)), but the text does not say so.

C013 item 3 and the supplement do not restate the general preamble of Example 4.6.11 (uniformly integrable, almost surely convergent X_n give E(X_n|F) -> E(X|F) in L^1); it follows from thm:p15-vitali-convergence and thm:p15-changing-conditional-limits (1) with a constant filtration.

Notation departs from Durrett in places (D_n for his F_n in Exercises 4.6.2-4.6.3; xi_i for Z_i in Exercise 4.6.1; B_n, C_n for Y_n, Z_n in Example 4.6.11). The supplement records the correspondence for Exercise 4.6.1 and for backwards martingales, but not for Example 4.6.11.
